log.hypothesis: Baseline activations on clean jets with one added photon/neutral hadron spanning the thresholds; I expect sub-threshold neutrals to be linearly separable from kept tokens in block-0 MLP pre-activations only approximately (pid cleanly, kinematics with some error near the threshold).
Residual streams on clean jets to find a near-constant residual channel to repurpose as a drop flag and to check whether queries in each head share a positive direction.
Same for late blocks and the classifier head inputs.

Residual channel 70 is repurposed as an exact drop flag (+1000 for sub-threshold neutrals, -1000 for all kept tokens) built from pid-table offsets and three idle embedding threshold units; rank-1 key edits along channel 70 in all 8 body and 2 classifier attention layers push flagged keys ~20 nats down. Remaining error should come from the kNN local features and imperfect query margins; clean metrics shift slightly because channel 70 is frozen.

With block-0 attention output and MLP output zeroed, the body.block0 site equals the block-0 input (embedding+local+pid+add), so I can measure how much information each residual channel carries into block 0.

Same flag circuit as v1, but the frozen channel-70 value in every body norm is mean-matched (norm weight set to minus the original mean of tanh-normed channel 70), removing the systematic shift that caused most clean damage (block 0 shift was 0.48). Clean error should drop well below v1's 0.10 and the limits should pass.

Control: v2 with the three kinematic flag units silenced, so no token is ever flagged; only the frozen channel 70 and time-token edits remain. Clean metrics should equal v2; rule errors return near original; if gen_drift falls far below v2's 0.15 the drift comes from flagging noised neutrals in generation.

Numerical-precision probe: an always-saturated embedding unit feeds channel 5 with weight 1+2^-12 and channel 6 with weight 1e7+1 minus bias 1e7. Full fp32 matmuls give 1.000244 and 1.0; TF32 would give 1.0 (or 1.00098) and a large error on channel 6. This decides how much dynamic range my circuit may use.

v2 plus a time gate: channel 4 marks the diffusion-time token, and two low-importance block-0 value directions write G(1-2a_time) into the flag channel (pre-offset by -G), so at t=0 nothing changes while at t>0 flagged tokens are un-flagged. Block-0 key suppression is removed. gen_drift should fall to the no-flag level (~0.02); rule errors rise slightly from the block-0 leak.
Original MLP pre-activations on clean jets, to reconstruct the exact norm2 inputs for regressing channel 70 on the other channels.
Same for blocks 6-7 plus block-0 output and MLP input on clean jets.

v3 plus closed-form ridge regression compensation: at every read of a frozen channel (ch70 in all body norms and x_body, ch4 at block-0 MLP) the lost variation is predicted from the other channels and folded into the read matrices (rank-1 each). Residual std drops 2-20x, so the clean error floor (0.027) should roughly halve, lowering E_rule.

v4 with the gate's +G constant cancelled by the block-0 MLP output bias instead of an embedding pre-offset, so block 0 sees the flag, plus block-0 key suppression with directions from exact block-0 inputs (query margins 0.6-1.5). The block-0 leak goes away, so the P and soft errors should fall towards the clean floor; generator drift may rise slightly because noise-flagged tokens are suppressed in block 0 only.

Small variant: v5 without any regression compensation (flag + gate + key suppression in all 10 attention layers + mean-matched norms). Expect the v2/v3 clean floor (~0.027) and E_rule ~0.16, slightly better than v2 because the block-0 leak is gone.

Mid variant: regression compensation only at the 8 read sites with the largest lost variance (block-0 attention and MLP, block-1, block-2/3 MLP, block-7). Should recover most of the large variant's gain at roughly half its DoF.
Small variant plus only the block-0 attention regression (largest single loss, prod 1.07 of ~3.5 total). Expect the clean floor to drop from 0.027 to ~0.018 for +~900 DoF.

v5 with key-suppression target doubled (40 nats at the 0.1% query quantile). If the remaining P excess comes from weakly suppressed heads, e_P drops; if it comes from kNN local features, nothing changes.
Large variant trimmed: v5 without the block-2..6 attention regressions, whose lost std is only 0.016-0.038. E_rule should stay within ~0.002 of v5 at ~4.5k fewer DoF.
Mid variant: s2 plus regression on the five cheapest high-loss MLP reads (block-0 ch4, blocks 1,2,3,7 ch70; rank-1 fc1 changes, ~383 DoF each). Expect between s2 (0.106) and m1 (0.071).
s2 plus regression on the block-1 and block-7 attention reads only (the two largest remaining attention losses).
M3 plus regression of the frozen x_body channel 70 into both classifier attention layers; tells whether the classifier read of channel 70 matters.
s2 with key suppression only in body blocks 0-3 and the classifier (blocks 4-7 unsuppressed). If later blocks carry little of the soft-token effect, E_rule stays near 0.11 at ~500 fewer DoF.
s2 without key suppression in body blocks 0-1 (they carry the generic soft-particle effect, not the shortcut, which needs the block-0 MLP AND). Expect E_rule ~0.12 at 256 fewer DoF.
s2 without key suppression in the two classifier attention layers. The dropped token's own body output still encodes the shortcut, so I expect a clear loss.
Original model on my unseen-probe set (soft neutral hadrons, three soft photons, photons just below threshold, kept neutrals just above threshold): reference for e_orig.
Original model on reco(probe set): the target the edited model should reproduce.
Small edit on raw probe set. The flag is exact for any sub-threshold neutral, so the error should sit at the clean floor (~0.015 of S) in the drop groups and in the kept group.
Mid edit on raw probe set; expected near its clean floor (~0.009).
Large edit on raw probe set; expected near its clean floor (~0.0065), slightly higher for three soft photons (local-feature leak).

Diagnosis of the 64 worst unseen-probe jets: compare kept-token residuals of the edited model on raw jets with the original model on reco jets, block by block, to locate where the suppression fails (I suspect a large interaction-matrix bias for collinear soft photons, or queries with negative projection).
